_about: How names and recurring terms are written in this language. Every translation follows this file, so a name is always spelled the same way. Names are written by sound, never translated (the author's rule). The spellings here are first versions based on the written names: the author's own pronunciation is recorded in Legacy/Behind The Scenes/World Lore/Word Pronunciation/Unique Words Pronounciation.wav, so correct any spelling here and later translations will follow it. Add new names the first time they are translated.
rule: Story names stay exactly as in English, as in Portuguese, Spanish, Malay and German. That includes coined world terms written as names: creatures, plants, items, nari gels, spells, factions, guilds, places, ranks and coins (Wood People, Sand Worms, Fost Stone, Nari Refresher, Red Winga, Sapphire, Pearl). Plain words around them are translated into Vietnamese and follow Vietnamese word order, head word first (gel nari, đá nari, bom nari, giao diện Darfaries, nhà mạo hiểm Sapphire). Kingdoms read 'Vương quốc Sanbi', guards 'lính canh Forway'. The currency balls is 'bi' (marbles/balls), which keeps the double meaning; the rank follows it (bi Sapphire, bi Pearl). The unit timehunk stays as is. The reader is 'bạn' and the author speaks as 'tôi', matching the author's casual voice; profanity is kept. Dates put the day first: '994 A.G. Adrian 6th' becomes '6 Adrian 994 A.G.'; with a weekday, 'Gannday, 14 Paulin 1039 A.G.'. Gregorian dates read '1 tháng 6 năm 2020'. 'Sanbi shit!' (the Sanbi oath) is always 'Hồn Sanbi già ơi!' ('Old Sanbi soul!'), the author's rule; 'Sanbi shit out of luck' becomes 'chỉ còn biết xui thôi, hồn Sanbi già ơi!'. Standard Vietnamese spelling.
